Title: Debug logs expose tokens & user data
Description: console.log statements print req.cookies (access tokens), Authorization headers, and full req.user JSON including tenant_id and role on every request
Impact: Access tokens, refresh tokens, tenant info, and roles are visible in server logs. If logs are accessible, full session takeover is possible
Fix / Recommendation: Remove all [Auth Debug] console.log statements before production. Search: grep "Auth Debug" in auth.middleware.js

Title: Employee profile IDOR — any employee ID accepted
Description: getEmployeeProfile(selectedId) fetches full profile without verifying the requester owns or manages that employee. All dependent data (attendance, leave, documents, performance, assets) loaded with no frontend authz check
Impact: Employee A can view Employee B's private profile, salary, leave history, and documents if backend tenant scoping is absent or incomplete
Fix / Recommendation: Backend must validate employee_id belongs to requester's tenant and the requester has manager/admin role. Frontend should guard using hasPermission() before calling the service.

Title: Messages / Tasks / Support routes have NO AdminModuleGate
Description: <Messages />, <NotificationCenter />, <TaskManagement />, <TaskDetails />, and support-management routes are rendered directly without wrapping in AdminModuleGate or any permission check
Impact: Users can deep-link or navigate to restricted modules regardless of their plan or role. Task and support UIs are accessible to employees
Fix / Recommendation: Wrap each route in AdminModuleGate with the correct module key. Example: <AdminModuleGate module="messages"><Messages /></AdminModuleGate>

Title: Access token and full user object stored in localStorage
Description: hris_token (access token) stored in localStorage (TOKEN_KEY). Full hris_auth_user object also stored. localStorage is readable by any JavaScript on the page
Impact: XSS attack on any page steals access token and full user session (role, tenant, email, permissions). No expiry enforced by storage layer
Fix / Recommendation: Remove localStorage token fallback; rely solely on httpOnly cookies. If fallback needed, use sessionStorage only. Enforce strict CSP headers.

Title: Login lockout not enforced before password comparison
Description: Central resolution path verifies the password inline (line ~1338) then enforces lockout later (line 1413). A locked account that already passed password comparison during central resolution still receives a login token
Impact: Locked accounts can successfully log in if the central resolution path is taken, bypassing account lockout entirely
Fix / Recommendation: Move enforceAdminLockout() to BEFORE any password comparison call. Enforce lockout as the very first gate after finding the user record.

Title: MFA can be disabled with null/empty code
Description: disable() function checks if code is missing only AFTER confirming MFA is enabled. Route declares code as optional (auth.routes.js body('code').optional()). If code is empty, the check throws — but the NOT-enabled path returns success silently
Impact: Attacker with account access (e.g., via session hijack) sends a disable-MFA request with no code and the account's MFA is removed, downgrading security to password-only
Fix / Recommendation: Make code mandatory when row.mfa_enabled = true. Add: if (row.mfa_enabled && !code) throw ApiError.badRequest('Enter your current 6-digit code'). Remove optional() from route validator.

Title: Employee portal lockout bypassed when portal_enabled = false
Description: enforceEmployeeLockout() is called inside the if (employeePortalActive) block. Accounts with portal_enabled = false skip lockout entirely — an attacker can brute-force these accounts indefinitely
Impact: Disabled-portal employee accounts have no brute-force protection. An attacker who re-enables portal later inherits a full attempt counter reset
Fix / Recommendation: Move enforceEmployeeLockout() outside the portal_enabled check so lockout is always enforced regardless of portal status.

Title: Password reset OTP not deleted immediately after first use
Description: verifyOTP() may mark the record as used but the SELECT query on lines 392-399 re-reads the same record. Between verifyOTP() marking expiry and the DELETE, another concurrent request could reuse the same OTP
Impact: Race condition allows OTP replay within expiry window. Two concurrent reset requests with the same code could both succeed
Fix / Recommendation: Replace two-step verify+fetch with a single atomic DELETE … RETURNING so the record is removed in one query. Example: DELETE FROM password_resets WHERE email=$1 AND otp_code=$2 RETURNING tenant_id, user_type

Title: MFA challenge JWT signed with same secret as access tokens
Description: issueMfaChallenge() uses env.JWT.secret (the main access-token secret) to sign the MFA intermediate token. No attempt counter or per-token rate limiting
Impact: If JWT secret is leaked, attackers can forge valid MFA challenge tokens and bypass 2FA completely. No rate limiting means brute-force of TOTP codes is possible
Fix / Recommendation: Use a dedicated env.JWT.mfaSecret for signing MFA tokens. Store issued MFA challenge tokens in Redis with attempt counters (max 5 attempts before invalidation).

Title: Timing-based email enumeration in forgot-password
Description: requestPasswordReset() iterates all active tenants when user not found in index (lines 194-222). This O(N) scan takes significantly longer than the fast-path for valid emails, leaking whether an email exists
Impact: Attacker measures response time: fast response (~50ms) = email not found; slow response (~500ms) = email found in some tenant. Enables org-wide email harvesting
Fix / Recommendation: Add a fixed artificial delay (200-300ms minimum response time) regardless of whether the email was found. Use: await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 250))

Title: No session invalidation after password change
Description: changePassword() updates the hash and returns success but does NOT revoke existing refresh tokens for that user. All active sessions (on other devices/browsers) remain valid with the old refresh token
Impact: If account is compromised and owner changes password, attacker's existing session persists. Account takeover survives a password reset
Fix / Recommendation: After updating password hash, run: UPDATE public.refresh_tokens SET revoked = TRUE WHERE user_id = $1 AND role = $2 to invalidate all active sessions.

Title: No CSRF protection on state-changing auth endpoints
Description: POST /auth/logout, POST /auth/change-password, POST /auth/forgot-password lack CSRF tokens. recaptcha middleware only covers /login
Impact: Cross-site form submissions can force logout, trigger password change emails, or lock accounts
Fix / Recommendation: Implement double-submit cookie CSRF protection or use the Synchronizer Token Pattern on all POST/PUT/DELETE auth endpoints.

Title: Impersonation codes stored in-memory with no audit log
Description: issueImpersonationCode() and redeemImpersonationCode() use a plain JS Map. No database record. No log of who impersonated, which tenant, from what IP, or when
Impact: Server restart wipes all pending codes. Multi-instance deployments break impersonation entirely. No forensic trail if a tenant account is accessed improperly by support
Fix / Recommendation: Store impersonation codes in the database (public.impersonation_codes table) with: code_hash, generated_by, tenant_id, generated_at, redeemed_at, redeemed_from_ip. Log every redemption.

Title: Stripe session_id passed in URL query param
Description: Payment confirmation reads session_id from ?session_id=xxx in the URL. URL params are saved in browser history, server logs, and referrer headers before setSearchParams removes them
Impact: Stripe session ID exposed in browser history and logs. Could allow replay attacks or session hijacking in Stripe payment flows
Fix / Recommendation: Pass session confirmation via POST body or use Stripe's redirect_url mechanism that hashes the session. Never embed financial session IDs in URLs.

Title: Refresh token JTI stored unhashed in database
Description: issueRefreshToken() inserts the raw UUID jti directly into public.refresh_tokens. If the database is breached, all active JTIs are exposed
Impact: Attacker with DB read access can forge valid refresh tokens by crafting JWTs with known JTIs signed with any captured JWT secret
Fix / Recommendation: Hash JTI before storing: const hashedJti = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(jti).digest('hex'). Compare hashes on verification.

Title: No dedicated OTP generation rate limit
Description: POST /auth/forgot-password uses the generic authLimiter. No per-email rate limit on OTP generation
Impact: Attacker can flood a target's email inbox or brute-force the 6-digit OTP within the general rate limit window
Fix / Recommendation: Add email-keyed rate limiter: max 3 OTP requests per email per 15 minutes. Key generator: req => req.body.email

Title: Superadmin role detection fragile and case-sensitive
Description: Role read from localStorage, string-cleaned with replace(/[_\s]/g, ''), compared case-sensitively to 'superadmin'. If role stored with different casing or format, wrong refresh flow is used
Impact: Admin users might get employee token-refresh path, causing 401 loops or wrong cookie clearing on logout
Fix / Recommendation: Normalize role to lowercase before comparison. Centralise role resolution in AuthContext rather than re-reading localStorage in api.js.

Title: API URL falls back to HTTP localhost if env var missing
Description: Both api.js and Login.jsx default to http://localhost:5000 when VITE_API_URL is unset. Login.jsx has its own separate copy of this fallback (inconsistency)
Impact: If deployed without env var, all auth requests go over plain HTTP to localhost — credentials sent unencrypted. Two separate fallback definitions may diverge
Fix / Recommendation: Remove the localhost fallback or make it throw in production builds. Remove the duplicate fallback in Login.jsx and import the base URL from api.js.

Title: refreshAccessProfile has no debounce or cancellation
Description: Interval timer fires every 3 minutes calling refreshAccessProfile(). No AbortController. Previous request still in-flight when next fires
Impact: Stale responses can overwrite fresh state. If the user logs out during a refresh, the completed refresh re-populates auth state causing ghost sessions
Fix / Recommendation: Add AbortController per refresh call. Cancel previous controller before starting a new one. Clear interval on logout.

Title: Messages module hardcoded as always-available
Description: hasModule('messages') returns true unconditionally (line 232). system-settings returns true for any admin regardless of allowedModules
Impact: Cannot restrict message access to specific roles or tenants. Admin always sees settings even if not in their plan
Fix / Recommendation: Remove hardcoded true return. Route both through the standard planModuleKeys / allowedModules check path.

Title: Employee profile service accepts arbitrary IDs
Description: getEmployeeProfile(id) directly calls GET /employees/${id} with no frontend ownership check. Called from multiple locations with user-supplied IDs
Impact: Any logged-in user who knows another employee's ID can fetch their complete profile data if the backend does not enforce ownership
Fix / Recommendation: Frontend should verify id === currentUser.employeeId or currentUser has admin/manager role before calling. Consider passing user role context to the service.

Title: Dashboard loads up to 500 employee records client-side
Description: fetchAdminDashboard() calls listEmployees({ limit: 500 }) to compute birthdays and anniversaries. All employee names, emails, join dates loaded into browser memory
Impact: Excessive data fetched client-side. Employees' PII in browser memory and potentially in browser devtools
Fix / Recommendation: Move birthday/anniversary calculation to a dedicated backend API endpoint that returns only counts or relevant names within a narrow date window.

Title: Exit records stored unencrypted in localStorage as fallback
Description: createResignation and getLocalExitForms read/write sensitive exit/termination data (reason, settlement) to localStorage fallback store
Impact: Termination reason and settlement details visible to any script on the page and persist after logout until manually cleared
Fix / Recommendation: Remove localStorage exit record fallback. If offline support is required, use IndexedDB with encryption (e.g., via CryptoKey API).

Title: Password expiry not enforced at login
Description: passwordExpiryDays is defined in password policy settings but the login flow never checks if a user's password has exceeded that age
Impact: Users continue using expired passwords indefinitely despite the policy being configured. Policy setting has no effect
Fix / Recommendation: On successful credential verification, query password_changed_at. If (now - password_changed_at) > expiry_days, return { passwordExpired: true } to force a password reset before issuing tokens.

Title: Missing security headers on auth responses
Description: Auth endpoints do not set X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, or Strict-Transport-Security
Impact: Missing HSTS leaves auth endpoints accessible over HTTP. Missing X-Frame-Options allows clickjacking of login page. Missing nosniff allows MIME-type sniffing attacks
Fix / Recommendation: Add helmet.js middleware globally or add these headers in auth controller responses. Verify HSTS is set on the load balancer/nginx if using TLS termination there.

Title: Impersonation code generation has no TTL enforcement in multi-server setup
Description: pruneExpiredCodes() only runs lazily on next issueImpersonationCode() call. In low-traffic periods, expired codes remain in memory
Impact: Expired impersonation codes linger in memory longer than the 5-minute TTL. Harmless in single-server but misleading if code leaks
Fix / Recommendation: Switch to DB-backed storage (AUTH-013 fix). Until then, run pruneExpiredCodes() on a setInterval every 60 seconds.

Title: Salary inputs have no client-side bounds validation
Description: net_salary, earnings, deductions sent to backend without checking for negative values, non-numeric input, or unrealistically large numbers
Impact: Backend may accept or reject silently. Users can inadvertently submit negative salaries or overflow values
Fix / Recommendation: Add min=0 and max=9999999 constraints on salary number inputs. Validate totals before submission.

Title: Silent error swallowing in data loads
Description: catch(() => setEmployees([])) and missing try-catch on /admin/documents leave users seeing empty lists with no explanation
Impact: Users cannot distinguish between "no data" and "failed to load". Support and debugging are severely hampered
Fix / Recommendation: Show a toast or inline error message on catch. Log error details to console in development. Never swallow errors silently in catch blocks.
